evals.prompt: I closed claude in a directory that had a running session by mistake, how can I find where I was and what session I was in?
evals.expected_output: Identifies the most recently closed session(s) other than the current one, giving directory, session id, last active time, last thing the user said, and a resume command.

evals.prompt: which claude session was I in when I asked about scott's email? I think it was a week or two ago. give me the command to get back into it
evals.expected_output: Finds the single pipeline-planning session containing the prompt 'Do you have scotts email?', reports its directory, id and last active time, quotes the prompt, and gives a resume command.

evals.prompt: show me all the claude code sessions I've had across all my projects in the last 2 weeks, when each was last active, and the last thing I said in each
evals.expected_output: A numbered shortlist covering every project directory with sessions in the window, each with last active time and the last meaningful user prompt (not 'exit'), sorted newest first. No session ids or resume commands inside a markdown table; if ids are shown they are on their own lines or in code blocks.

evals.prompt: I closed the terminal on my techtrip-skills session by accident. Give me the command to get back into it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies the newest session in the techtrip-skills directory and gives a single fenced code block containing 'cd <dir> && claude --continue' (since it is the newest there), mentions 'claude --resume <id>' as the exact alternative, and does not put the id or command in a table.

evals.prompt: which of my sessions from this week were in workspace-ai? I'll pick one and then I want the resume command on my clipboard
evals.expected_output: Phase one: a numbered shortlist (time, directory, quoted last prompt) without ids, offered through the AskUserQuestion picker or a prose question. After the pick: the session id on its own line, the resume command in a code block, and the script run with --copy <id-prefix> so the command is on the clipboard, reporting which tool copied it.
